paths.description: Homepage: primary news/score discovery template; tested desktop, 360px mobile, dark, reduced-motion, forced-colors, performance, privacy, network and memory.
Current sports article: representative content/reading and metadata template.
Botafogo team landing page: representative section/listing template.
Completed Corinthians v Remo match: representative score/video surface.
Unknown route: representative HTTP/error recovery state.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a white/light surface, visually identical to light mode.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark at the root and retint page tokens with light-dark() or prefers-color-scheme.

findings.summary: Loading skeleton animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, 12 one-second textSkeletton/bg-skeleton-box animations remained running; only header/dropdown transitions were disabled.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential skeleton and entrance animations inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The rendered CSS probe found zero view-transition rules across the homepage UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document and cross-document View Transitions for route and major state changes, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: A large cookie notice obscures primary content on load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the notice covering the lead story; on mobile it consumes roughly the lower third of the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface with clear choices and light-dismiss where legally appropriate.

findings.summary: Overlay UI is implemented as custom role dialogs rather than native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found 3 role=dialog elements but zero dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows and popover for transient UI, preserving focus management and declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: The article template breaks mobile reflow.
findings.evidence: At a 360px viewport the article layout reported scrollWidth 994px, innerWidth 994px, and 634px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed desktop widths and use intrinsic/fluid sizing so article content reflows to the visual viewport.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport styling without container queries.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found zero @container rules across a homepage with cards reused in horizontal strips and content grids.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container-type to reusable card regions and size-aware @container rules for local adaptation.

findings.summary: Some interactive targets are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: The target probe found visible 22×22px buttons, a 16×16px close button, and several 17–20px-high links.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 for primary touch controls, while retaining visible focus.

findings.summary: The homepage misses key loading and responsiveness thresholds.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.4s, TBT 1,320ms, CLS 0.125, and performance score 0.37; the trace independently measured LCP 4.95s and TBT 1,028.56ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reserve layout space, and defer/chunk non-critical scripts and third-party work.

findings.summary: Late content causes substantial layout shifts across templates.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.407 on home, 0.209 on article, and 0.152 on team pages; all exceed the 0.1 good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions for images, ad slots, cookie UI, and dynamic modules; stabilize font and skeleton geometry.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded 9 long tasks, a 779ms longest task, and 1,028.56ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Split long tasks, defer analytics/ad work, and schedule non-critical work by priority.

findings.summary: The network payload and dependency graph are excessive.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 459 requests and 15.94MB transferred, including 100 scripts (13.21MB) and 52 stylesheets; Lighthouse flagged LCP discovery and dependency chains.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse dependency chains, cache static assets, defer non-critical styles/scripts, and prioritize only critical resources.

findings.summary: Third-party and script payloads dominate the page load.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 447 third-party requests and 15.78MB third-party transfer, including 1.58MB from Google Tag Manager and 10.41MB from s3.glbimg.com.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit tags and bundles, remove duplicate/unused code, and load optional integrations only after intent or consent.

findings.summary: Accessible names and image alternatives are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-alt, label-content-name-mismatch, link-name, and list semantics; the homepage probe counted 402 unnamed links/buttons, and the article had 34 images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a stable accessible name, repair list semantics, and add meaningful or empty alt text as appropriate.

findings.summary: Some text fails minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse/axe color-contrast audit failed on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust text and background tokens to meet WCAG AA while preserving forced-colors support.

findings.summary: The accessibility tree and list structure are malformed.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed list structure and reported an ill-formed accessibility tree; the homepage also rendered an empty H1 in recon.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one meaningful H1, valid list children, semantic landmarks, and verify sequential focus order.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow and target sizing do not remain usable.
findings.evidence: The article overflows by 634px at 360px and multiple controls are below 24px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix article reflow and enlarge touch targets without disabling user zoom.

findings.summary: The page logs browser console errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s errors-in-console audit failed during a clean homepage load.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve uncaught exceptions and failed resource/runtime errors, and keep console monitoring in release checks.

findings.summary: Images lack explicit dimensions and use legacy formats.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 100/100 sampled images missing complete width/height dimensions and all 100 delivered as legacy PNG/JPEG/GIF rather than modern formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width and height/aspect-ratio and provide AVIF/WebP responsive sources while retaining fallbacks.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs, inspector issues, and BFCache blockers remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found one deprecated API warning, inspector issues, and three BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API use, fix DevTools issues, and eliminate unload/cache-control blockers that prevent BFCache.

findings.summary: Some links are unnamed or not crawlable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors and link-name; the page probe counted hundreds of controls/links without discernible text or labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real destination href values and descriptive visible/accessibility text for every navigational link.

findings.summary: Cookie and transport policy is weaker than expected.
findings.evidence: Headers lacked HSTS; the cookie audit found many cookies without Secure and widespread SameSite=None, including long-lived analytics identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable HSTS and mark every HTTPS cookie Secure with the narrowest viable SameSite and lifetime.

findings.summary: The page has an exceptionally large tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 91 third-party origins and 24 known tracker domains; HAR recorded 447 third-party requests and 15.78MB before an affirmative consent action.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to minimal collection, gate optional tags on informed consent, and consolidate or remove low-value vendors.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The response lacks HSTS, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy; CSP only sets frame-ancestors and upgrade-insecure-requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strict HSTS, a restrictive Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and expand CSP beyond framing/upgrade directives.

findings.summary: The cookie notice presents only “Prosseguir” and no equivalent reject/manage choice.
findings.evidence: DOM evidence shows links to policies plus one primary Prosseguir button, while trackers and identifiers load before that action.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer equally prominent accept, reject, and manage choices, and delay optional tracking until a valid selection.

findings.summary: Images are not delivered in resource-efficient formats or with stable sizing.
findings.evidence: All 100 sampled images were legacy formats and none had complete width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP sources at display-appropriate sizes and declare dimensions.

findings.summary: The page performs disproportionate network and main-thread work.
findings.evidence: A single load used 459 requests, 15.94MB transfer, 9 trace long tasks, and more than one second of blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant scripts/requests and defer background analytics, ads, and below-fold modules.

findings.summary: Third-party resources are disproportionate to the first-view content value.
findings.evidence: 447 of 459 requests and 15.78MB of 15.94MB transferred were classified as third-party; the tracker scan found 91 origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, lazy-load optional media, and require measurable value for each vendor.

findings.summary: The public news content is readable without JavaScript but intentionally blocks major AI crawlers and exposes no structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: Discoverability showed 76–83% raw-HTML content coverage, while robots.txt disallows CCBot, GPTBot, and Google-Extended and no WebMCP capability was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: If agent access is a product goal, define an explicit crawler policy and expose safe read/search capabilities through structured agent tools.

findings.summary: The initial JavaScript heap and DOM footprint are large for a news homepage.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contained 1,844,721 nodes and 116.1MB self size; a repeated scroll run ended at 1,893,993 nodes and 120.3MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile dominant constructors, reduce mounted offscreen content and third-party state, and enforce memory budgets.

taskList.title: Cut third-party scripts, tags and transfer before consent
Fix mobile article reflow, touch targets and layout stability
Repair accessible names, contrast and semantic structure
Replace blocking consent UI with semantic, balanced controls
